title: iPad (11th generation) screen replacement
diagnosis: It sounds like the cover glass and display assembly are cracked, so we'll replace the whole display assembly. This is a hard repair because the display is glued all around and the flex cables are fragile.
safety_notes: Wear safety glasses and cover the cracked glass with clear tape to contain shards.
Never pierce or bend the battery; keep tools away from the battery cells.

steps.title: Power off and tape the glass
steps.instruction: Hold the top button and a volume button, then slide to power off. Cover the whole cracked screen with clear packing tape.
steps.expected_visual_state: The iPad is dark and the screen is covered in overlapping strips of clear tape.
common_mistakes: Only sleeping the screen instead of powering off
Leaving glass uncovered so shards spread and cut fingers

steps.title: Heat the display edges
steps.instruction: Warm the display edges with a heat gun on low or an iOpener for 1 to 2 minutes. The edge should be hot to touch but not painful.
steps.expected_visual_state: A heat source is held near the edge of the iPad, with the iPad lying flat face up.
common_mistakes: Overheating one spot, which can damage the LCD or battery
Skipping heat and prying cold adhesive, which cracks the glass more

steps.title: Pry the display loose
steps.instruction: Attach the suction handle, lift slightly, and slide a plastic pick into the gap. Work around the edges slicing the adhesive, staying shallow.
steps.expected_visual_state: Several plastic picks sit in the gap around the edge, with the display lifting slightly from the shell.
common_mistakes: Inserting the pick deeper than a few millimetres and cutting flex cables
Prying near the corners where the glass can shatter
Using metal tools that can puncture the battery

steps.title: Open the display like a book
steps.instruction: Lift the display gently and rest it beside the shell without stretching its flex cables. Keep it supported.
steps.expected_visual_state: The display is lifted and resting open next to the shell, with the battery cells and logic board visible.
common_mistakes: Lifting too far and tearing the display flexes
Letting the display hang from its cables

steps.title: Disconnect the battery
steps.instruction: Unscrew the display cable bracket, then use a plastic spudger to pop the battery connector straight up.
steps.expected_visual_state: The bracket and its screws are set aside, and the battery connector is lifted off the logic board.
common_mistakes: Disconnecting the display cables before the battery
Prying the connector at an angle and bending its pins

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the old display
steps.instruction: Pop the display and digitizer connectors up with the spudger, then lift the old display away.
steps.expected_visual_state: The old display is fully separated and set aside, with the shell empty of display cables.
common_mistakes: Pulling the cables instead of lifting the connectors straight up

steps.title: Prepare the shell and fit the new display
steps.instruction: Clean off old adhesive with the plastic pick, apply new adhesive strips, and plug in the new display and digitizer connectors. Refit the bracket, then reconnect the battery.
steps.expected_visual_state: The new display lies near the shell with both connectors seated and the bracket screwed down.
common_mistakes: Leaving old adhesive or glass fragments in the shell
Reconnecting the battery before the display cables

steps.title: Close and test
steps.instruction: Press the display into the shell evenly around the edges. Power on and test touch across the whole screen and the top button.
steps.expected_visual_state: The iPad is closed with the edges flush, and the new screen shows the home screen and responds to touch.
common_mistakes: Closing it without testing first, so a bad connector means reopening it
Skipping testing the edges and corners for dead touch
